'''Doug Taylor''' was a Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]], listed as Red 4 FL from Lynnwood, Wa. The published fan table marks the slot Retired after Decipher's SWCCG run.

== Squadron listing ==

{| class="wikitable"
! Slot !! Town !! Status (fan table)
|-
| Red 4 FL || Lynnwood, Wa || Retired
|}

Decipher recruited volunteer Squadron Members in the 1990s to promote SWCCG locally (tournaments, demos, player support). "FL" is printed on some slots in the surviving tables; the tables do not spell out the abbreviation.

== Other sourced notes ==

Red 4 FL, Lynnwood, Washington. Named in Holland's 25 January 2002 announcement as a first Player Advocate for Gameplay Support (with Eric Olson).

== Jedi Knights TCG ==
Taylor playtested the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] (2001).<ref name="jkrules">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt ''Jedi Knights'' Trading Card Game rulebook (credits)], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010820125115/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt Internet Archive]</ref> As a Decipher Product Champion volunteer he reported on a Seattle pre-release event with about 40 players in April 2001.<ref name="jkprerelease">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/articles/042701storyC.html Pre-Release Parties Launch Jedi Knights!], decipher.com (April 2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010910003958/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/articles/042701storyC.html Internet Archive]</ref>
